description: Add a new heir to the estate. Use when the user wants to record a person who may inherit (spouse, child, stepchild, grandchild, parent, sibling, or other relative). Call as soon as you have a name and the user's description of the relationship — any wording is accepted.

address.description: Mailing address (free text, multi-line OK). Used for formal probate notice.

estate_id.description: The estate to act on. Call list_my_estates first to get this id.

is_deceased.description: Whether the heir is deceased (default false). Used for per stirpes inheritance.

is_divorced.description: For a spouse only: whether they are a divorced/former spouse (default false). A divorced spouse is recorded for a complete family picture but is not a surviving spouse and does not inherit under intestacy.

is_minor.description: Whether the heir is under 18. Required for every living heir except a spouse or parent — if the user hasn't said, ask them; never assume an adult.

name.description: Full legal name of the heir

notes.description: Free-text notes about this heir — context like whereabouts unknown, predeceased details, per-stirpes notes, disputes, or anything the user wants remembered. Multi-line OK.

parent_heir_id.description: ID of the parent heir if this person inherits through a deceased parent (e.g. grandchild whose parent predeceased the decedent). Omit otherwise.

relationship.description: Relationship to the deceased. Canonical values: spouse, child, stepchild, grandchild, parent, sibling, other. If the user's wording doesn't match one (e.g. 'half-brother', 'daughter-in-law', 'adult stepchild'), pass their wording as-is — it is normalized automatically. Never re-ask the user for a 'valid' relationship.

relationship_detail.description: The relationship exactly as the user described it, when it carries more than the canonical value (e.g. 'stepson', 'half-sister', 'goddaughter'). Shown on probate forms, so preserve the user's words.

name: create_heir
